what: The Z-Score Calculator turns a value into a z-score and a percentile, turns a z-score into probabilities and p-values, and finds the z-score for a given probability, such as the 1.96 used for 95% confidence.
A shaded normal curve shows exactly which area each answer refers to. It is built for statistics students, researchers checking a test result and anyone comparing a score with an average.
It uses accurate normal distribution formulas, not a printed table, and runs in your browser.
uses: See how far a mark is above the class average and what percentile it is.
Turn a test statistic into a one-tailed or two-tailed p-value.
Find critical values such as ±1.96 for 95% or ±2.576 for 99%.
Find what share of products fall between two limits.
Look up any area under the standard normal curve to many decimal places.
tutorial: Pick one of the four options: z-score from a value, probability from a z-score, z-score from a probability, or probability between two values.
Enter the value x, the mean μ and the standard deviation σ. The z-score is (x − μ) / σ, and you also get the percentile and p-values.
Enter z to get the area to the left, the area to the right and the two-tailed p-value.
Enter a probability (0.95) or percentile (95%) and say which area it is: left, right, middle or both tails. You get the matching z-score.
Enter two values with the mean and standard deviation to get the probability of falling between them.
The shaded part of the curve is the area of your answer. The table lists every related area for the same z-score.
features: Value to z, z to probability, probability to z and between two values.
Very small tail areas, such as for z = 8, are computed precisely.
Critical values for any confidence level or percentile.
Shows the left, right, middle or two-tailed area.

example.title: Worked example: a test score of 85
example.text: The class mean is 70 and the standard deviation is 10. z = (85 − 70) / 10 = 1.5. The area to the left of 1.5 is 0.933193, so 85 is at about the 93.3rd percentile. The area to the right is 0.066807 and the two-tailed p-value is 0.133614.

tips: A z-score of 0 is exactly average; most values (about 95%) lie between −1.96 and 1.96.
Percentiles assume the data follow a normal (bell-shaped) distribution; check this before relying on the result.
Use the two-tailed p-value when your test asks whether something is different in either direction.
For a confidence interval, choose 'in the middle' and enter the confidence level, such as 95%.
problems: It says the standard deviation must be greater than 0
A standard deviation cannot be 0 or negative. Check that you used the standard deviation, not the variance.
It must be strictly between 0 and 1 (or 0% and 100%).
My table gives a slightly different number
Printed tables round to four decimals; this tool computes the exact value.
